label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

report.summary: Outbox publications stalled for about 100 s while arrivals continued; delivery attempts failed with connection errors to the consumer, so notifications queued up and arrived late. Request path, pool and DB locks were healthy.

findings.claim: Outbox publication stopped from about 16:16:43 to about 16:18:23 while commits continued at ~26 per 10 s, so a backlog built (pending to 263, oldest age 126 s).
findings.reason: Per-bucket publications fell to 0 for ~10 buckets while arrivals stayed at 26; pending and oldest age grew steadily.

findings.claim: During the stall, delivery attempts failed with CONNECTION_FAILED (1508 of 1798) in under 2 ms, with no HTTP status. The consumer was refusing or unreachable.
findings.reason: Failures were instant with no consumer record, consistent with refused connections. Only 290 attempts succeeded, at ~71 ms.

findings.claim: The transfer API, DB pool and DB locking were not the bottleneck. Delay arises in the outbox-to-consumer hop.
findings.reason: Transfers returned 201 with p99 0.25 s and no 500s. Pool pending and timeouts were 0, and no blocking was sampled.

limitations: No consumer-side or network data explains why connections were refused (the consumer was probably down or restarting). The cause of the outage itself is not shown.
The delivery log listing covers only the earliest 100 of 1798 records, and the DB blocker and pool gauges are sampled, so short events could be missed.
next_checks: Check consumer process and listener logs for 127.0.0.1:18090 between about 16:16:43 and 16:18:23 for a crash, restart or port closure.
List delivery log records from 16:16:50 to 16:18:30 to confirm the failure window and retry backoff behaviour.

alternatives.reason: Catch-up reached 78-80 per bucket once publishing resumed, above the arrival rate, so the settings can drain the backlog. The stall coincides with connection failures.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox poller or batch settings (1 s poll, batch 20, 8 max attempts) limit the catch-up rate rather than the consumer outage.

alternatives.reason: Pool pending was 0 and there were no acquisition timeouts. No blocking sessions appeared in 75 samples.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database contention or pool exhaustion delayed outbox processing.

Look at delivery attempts after 16:18:20 to confirm they succeeded again and that the backlog drained.
